title: Asking questions: all the question words
goal: Build every kind of question — what, who, when, where, how, why, how much — and answer naturally.
bekal: the seven core question words and where they go in a sentence
yes/no questions without a question word, using *teu* or intonation
answering without repeating the whole sentence

dialogs.title: Paguneman — Questions from a neighbor
dialogs.intro: Rani is sweeping the porch when the next-door neighbor, Bu Éha, stops at the gate. Their first conversation is almost entirely questions.

lines.speaker: Bu Éha:
lines.text: Punten, Néng. Néng nu nembé ngontrak di bumi Bu Imas?
lines.id: Excuse me, Néng. Are you the one who's just moved into Bu Imas's house?
lines.literal: excuse-me, Néng. Néng who just renting at house Bu Imas?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: Yes, ma'am. My name is Rani.

lines.speaker: Bu Éha:
lines.id: What do you do in Bandung?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Abdi damel di kantor, di daérah Dago.
lines.id: I work in an office, in the Dago area.
lines.literal: I work at office, in area Dago.

lines.speaker: Bu Éha:
lines.id: When did you come to Bandung?

lines.speaker: Bu Éha:
lines.id: So, do you like it here?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: Very much. It's just that the air is cold.

lines.speaker: Bu Éha:
lines.id: Why aren't you wearing a jacket?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Poho, Bu. Hilap teu dicandak ti Jakarta.
lines.id: I forgot, ma'am. I forgot to bring one from Jakarta.
lines.literal: forgot, Ma'am. forgot not brought from Jakarta.

lines.speaker: Bu Éha:
lines.text: Saha waé nu di bumi téh, Néng nyalira?
lines.id: Who all lives in the house — are you on your own?
lines.literal: who all who in house [téh], Néng alone?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Sareng Néng Sari. Sadayana opat urang.
lines.id: With Néng Sari. Four of us altogether.
lines.literal: with Néng Sari. all four persons.

notes: **Naha** = why (same in lemes and loma). A more casual form: **kunaon**. Both go at the start of the sentence. ⚠️ In formal questions *naha* can also mark a yes/no question, like "is it that…?": *Naha leres kitu?* = is that really so?
**Nyalira** = alone, on your own (lemes); loma: **sorangan**. *Néng nyalira?* = "Are you on your own?" — a question neighbors ask newcomers all the time.
**Hilap** = forget (lemes); loma: **poho**. Notice that Rani uses both in one answer — natural, and common in real conversation.
**Ngangge** = to wear, use (lemes); loma: **maké**. *Teu ngangge jakét* = not wearing a jacket.
**Hawa** = air, weather. *Hawana tiis* = the air is cold. Bandung's cool weather is a conversation opener that never fails.

**Ngan** = only; but, it's just that. It introduces an exception: *betah pisan, ngan hawana tiis*. The lemes form is **mung**. It differs from *waé*, which means "just" in the sense of limiting a choice.

grammars.title: The question words and where they go
body: Sundanese question words can come at the start or at the end of the sentence; both are natural. The only thing to watch is the lemes/loma form of the words around them.
after: The good news: almost all question words are **the same** at both levels. Only the words around them change. *Ti mana asalna?* is identical in both; what makes it polite is whether you add *Bu* and lemes words to the rest.

⚠️ Sundanese has no question marker like English "do/does" or word-order inversion. Yes/no questions are made by adding **teu** (loma) or **henteu** (lemes) at the end — like a tag "…or not?": *Betah teu?* = do you like it (or not)? *Tos tuang henteu?* = have you eaten yet?
The second, equally common way is **intonation alone**: *Néng ti Jakarta?* said with a rising voice is already a question, with no extra words — just like "You're from Jakarta?" in English.

blocks.text: Sundanese answers are almost always **short**. Repeating the whole question sounds stiff, like a textbook drill. *Ti mana asalna?* is answered simply *Ti Jakarta*, not *Abdi asalna ti Jakarta*.

blocks.title: The most useful short answers
items: **Kitu** — that's right (agreeing with what was said)

blocks.text: As a newcomer you will hear these ten questions over and over from neighbors, workmen, and people in the *angkot* (minibus). Prepare your answers once and the rest flows.

head: Question
Meaning
Ready-made answer
rows: How long have you been in Bandung?
Do you often go back to Jakarta?

blocks.text: ⚠️ Question seven may feel too personal to many Western ears, but in Sundanese custom it's a normal part of getting acquainted — not prying at all. A short answer with a smile is enough, and you're under no obligation to explain further.

blocks.title: Asking back politely
items: **Ari Ibu nyalira?** — And you, ma'am? (returning the question)
**Punten, upami kenging terang…** — Excuse me, if I may ask…
**Punten badé naros sakedik.** — Excuse me, may I ask something? (*naros* = ask, lemes)
**Hapunten upami lepat naros.** — Sorry if that was the wrong thing to ask.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right question word.
Turn each statement into a yes/no question by adding teu or henteu.
Answer each question with a natural short answer.
Put the words in the right order to make a question.

answers: Saha — Iraha — di mana — Naha — Sabaraha — Kumaha
Betah teu di Bandung? — Tiasa basa Sunda henteu? — Tos tuang henteu? — Aya cai teu? — Lada teu sambelna? — Sumping isukan henteu?
Ti Jakarta. — Sakedik, nembé diajar. — Nembé dua minggu. — Muhun, nyalira. — Betah pisan. — Sabulan sakali.
Ti mana asalna? — Naon damelna? — Iraha sumpingna? — Betah teu di dieu? — Saha jenenganana?
